item.title: Indianapolis Swish festival to bring music, dance, artworks during Final Four
item.description: The Swish 2026 arts and culture festival will feature music, dance, visual art, food, and historical and theatrical programs from April 3-6 in downtown Indianapolis during the 2026 NCAA Men's Final Four.

item.title: Indiana health care providers oppose Medicaid cost-cutting proposal
item.description: The Indiana Family and Social Services Administration has proposed a change to its Medicaid 340B Drug Program, which would reduce a revenue source for many hospitals and clinics, while saving the state government millions of dollars. Providers worry the change could reduce access to care for underserved communities.

item.title: Gov. Braun says he might retain some Indiana Economic Development Foundation functions
item.description: Gov. Mike Braun says he may retain some of the functions of the now-dormant Indiana Economic Development Foundation.

item.title: Indianapolis 500 suite ticket holders get sneak peek at May culinary delights
item.description: Indianapolis Motor Speedway hosted a preview event for suite ticket holders to showcase the food offerings available during the monthlong racing extravaganza in May.

item.title: Former Colts wide receiver T.Y. Hilton announces retirement
item.description: T.Y. Hilton, former Colts wide receiver, announced his retirement from the NFL after playing for the Colts from 2012-2021 and the Cowboys in 2022, having achieved 5 Pro Bowls and leading the NFL in receiving yards in 2016.

item.title: Jury convicts man of 2024 murder of sound tech at Indiana Convention Center
item.description: A jury convicted Brian Fulton, 34, of Indianapolis, of murdering Alan Ray Gosnell, a sound and lighting technician, at the Indiana Convention Center in September 2024.

item.title: Planned Parenthood to close 2 Indianapolis sites, consolidate at Georgetown clinic
item.description: Planned Parenthood is closing two Indianapolis clinics and merging operations into its Georgetown location due to funding cuts and rising costs.

item.title: Sabey Data Centers’ $4 billion project in Indianapolis gets OK to build
item.description: Despite strong opposition from some residents, the Metropolitan Development Commission has approved a proposal for a $4 billion data center to be built on the southeast side of Indianapolis. Construction was expected to start this year, and the first building could be completed by 2028.

item.title: Trump threatens retaliation if Iran attacks Qatar again
item.description: Qatar said that Iranian missile attacks damaged liquefied natural gas sites in the country, causing sizable fires and extensive further damage, while Israel killed Iran's intelligence minister and reportedly attacked an Iranian offshore natural gas field in the Persian Gulf, causing Iran to retaliate with missile strikes against Israel and its allies in the region.

item.title: At least 8 injured as pickup crashes into Chili’s restaurant in Martinsville
item.description: Eight people were injured March 18, 2026, after a pickup crashed into a Chili's restaurant in Martinsville, Indiana.
